citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
Expired medications were located within the controlled substances lockbox. The medications were stored in the same
holding containers as the non-expired medications. The attending veterinarian stated, prior to opening the lockbox, “There
are expired controlled substances within the lockbox, but I haven’t had a chance to take them to be disposed.” When the
attending veterinarian opened the lockbox, APHIS officials had asked where the expired medication was stored, because
there was not a box labeled for expired medications. The attending veterinarian stated she “kept the expired and non-
expired medications together, so that the same medication label matched the storage box medication name.” There were
some boxes of medication that had "Expired" written across the box, but others that were expired were not labeled until
they were pointed out to the facility representative. At that time, the facility representative began labeling medications as
“Expired” as APHIS officials were taking out the expired medications from the lockbox. The expired medications that were
found within the lockbox included: Alfaxan (exp. 01/2026), Euthasol (05/2026), Euthasol (09/2026) Trophadine (12/2025),
Placadine (06/2026), and Dormosedan Gel (10/2025).
The storage of both non-expired and expired medications in the same medicine box can lead to the accidental use of
expired product. Expired medications should not be used, as their effectiveness significantly decreases when expired and
may cause a failure in treatment. An exhibitor shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that
include the availability of appropriate facilities, personnel, equipment, and services.
Corrected at the time of inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
